title: Frames in Four Lanes
tag: One classroom move, under three minutes, for the teacher who teaches content, not English.

beats.say: Six Moves, from EL Publishing. Move two: sentence frames in four lanes.

chunks.text: Six Moves, from EL Publishing. Move two: sentence frames in four lanes.

beats.say: You ask the class a good question: why is this a plant cell and not an animal cell? Hands go up. The same four hands. Your English learners know the answer. They don't have the sentence to put it in.

chunks.text: You ask the class a good question: why is this a plant cell and not an animal cell? Hands go up.
The same four hands. Your English learners know the answer. They don't have the sentence to put it in.

beats.say: A sentence frame is the sentence with the content missing. This is a blank cell. The frame carries the grammar, so the student only has to supply the idea. A level-one student says: this is a plant cell. That's a correct spoken answer in academic English, from a student who arrived last month.

chunks.text: A sentence frame is the sentence with the content missing. This is a blank cell.
The frame carries the grammar, so the student only has to supply the idea.
A level-one student says: this is a plant cell.
That's a correct spoken answer in academic English, from a student who arrived last month.

beats.say: Here's the move. Don't post one frame. Post four, one per lane, and let students pick.

chunks.text: Here's the move. Don't post one frame. Post four, one per lane, and let students pick.

beats.say: Lane one, for a level one or two: one blank, and a word bank next to it.

chunks.text: Lane one, for a level one or two: one blank, and a word bank next to it.

a: 2 · It is a plant cell because it has a ___.
beats.say: Lane two: a frame with a reason built in. It is a plant cell because it has a blank.

chunks.text: Lane two: a frame with a reason built in. It is a plant cell because it has a blank.

beats.say: Lane three, for a level three: I think blank because blank. Now they're building the sentence.

chunks.text: Lane three, for a level three: I think blank because blank. Now they're building the sentence.

beats.say: Lane four, for a level four and for your native speakers: although blank, the evidence shows blank. They would not say that on their own. With the frame, they will.

chunks.text: Lane four, for a level four and for your native speakers: although blank, the evidence shows blank.
They would not say that on their own. With the frame, they will.

beats.say: Students usually pick the right lane for themselves. When someone picks too low, you nudge: try lane three today.

chunks.text: Students usually pick the right lane for themselves.
When someone picks too low, you nudge: try lane three today.

a: Question + four frames on the board
Partner A talks, partner B says it back
You pick two or three to share
beats.say: Running it takes seven or eight minutes. The question and the four frames go on the board. Thirty seconds of silence to think. Partner A talks for a minute; partner B listens and says back one thing they heard. Switch. Then you pick two or three students to share with the class — you pick, so it isn't the same four hands.

Thirty seconds of silence to think.
Partner A talks for a minute; partner B listens and says back one thing they heard. Switch.

beats.say: The say-it-back step matters. If a level-one student says a word and their partner has to repeat it, the word was heard. It counted. Nobody got ignored.

chunks.text: The say-it-back step matters.
If a level-one student says a word and their partner has to repeat it, the word was heard. It counted.
Nobody got ignored.

beats.say: Without frames, you get four hands, a silent newcomer, and one-word answers from the students who could do more. With four lanes, everyone speaks academic English twice, the newcomer says a whole sentence, and your level fours are using although and the evidence shows.
